title: Optimal two-mode bosonic loss codes from finite group symmetry
authors: Argyris Giannisis Manes, Mahadevan Subramanian, Liang Jiang
abstract: Photon loss is a dominant noise process in bosonic quantum hardware, including superconducting cavities. Fixed-total-photon-number qubit encodings in two bosonic modes retain the loss-detection advantage of dual-rail qubits while supporting photon loss correction. Optimizing entanglement fidelity in this setting for $4\leq n\leq25$ over arbitrary encoders and decoders reveals finite-group structure in every best-found code: 11 correspond to two-dimensional irreducible representations and 11 to reducible ones. Motivated by this emergence, we derive the necessary-and-sufficient Knill-Laflamme conditions for arbitrary finite-group-invariant codes, reducing their construction to equations on representation multiplicity spaces. For every finite subgroup of $SU(2)$ and every tensor rank, we explicitly construct the minimum number of operators required to impose all corresponding loss-correction constraints. These results produce analytic counterparts to most numerical codes and predict constructions missed by the initial search. Exact MacWilliams-Farkas certificates show that our codes achieve the maximum possible loss distance in 21 of the 22 sectors, and we prove that the resulting distance bound is monotone in total photon number. Beyond the scan, we identify a binary-polyhedral sequence with photon number $n_d=\lceil(3d^2+1)/4\rceil$ and construct each corresponding code through distance $d=10$. To our knowledge, the constructed $(n,d)=(28,6),(49,8),(76,10)$ codes give the smallest reported $n$ for their respective distances; all members through $d=9$ attain the fixed-$n$ LP distance bound. Together, these constructions, certificates, and a symmetry-reduced constraint count provide evidence for an infinite code family conjectured to attain every distance at the minimum photon number.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theory for constructing optimal quantum error-correcting codes designed to combat photon loss in bosonic quantum hardware. By leveraging the mathematical framework of finite group symmetry and representation theory, the authors derive exact conditions for these codes. The results provide concrete, high-performance code constructions that advance the field toward achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation in photonic platforms.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of designing optimal quantum error-correcting codes (QEC) for bosonic systems that suffer from photon loss.
main_result: The authors derive a rigorous, group-theoretic framework to construct these codes, achieving maximum possible loss distance in most tested sectors and suggesting an infinite family of optimal codes.
method: The methodology combines representation theory (using finite subgroups of SU(2)) with advanced techniques like MacWilliams transforms and linear programming feasibility checks to constrain code construction.
model_or_system: The system is bosonic quantum hardware, specifically modeled using two bosonic modes constrained to a fixed total photon number subspace, relevant for superconducting cavities.
key_observables: Entanglement fidelity ($F_e$), loss distance ($d$), and the structure of the code projector relative to finite group representations.
important_parameters: Total photon number ($n$), code distance ($d$), and the symmetry group $G$ (finite subgroups of SU(2)).
main_assumptions: The initial optimization is biconvex, and the final conjecture regarding the infinite code family remains unproven.
figures_summary: Figures summarize the pipeline from numerical discovery of finite-group structure to representation-theoretic reduction and final certification via MacWilliams linear programs, comparing theoretical bounds to constructed code distances.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from numerical discovery of finite-group structure in optimal codes to deriving necessary-and-sufficient Knill-Laflamme conditions based on group invariance. It then develops the mathematical machinery using MacWilliams transforms and Farkas' Lemma to prove existence bounds and constructs explicit, optimal code families.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical structure (group theory) to the physical problem of quantum noise correction in photonic systems, offering concrete, provable constructions for hardware implementation.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Discovery, construction, and certification of fixed-excitation two-mode loss codes. (a) Symmetry-unconstrained bi-convex optimization of the encoder and recovery produces numerical codes with finite-group representation structure. (b) General representation-theoretic Knill–Laflamme reductions and sufficient loss-seed operators turn that structure into exact codes. (c) MacWilliams linear programs, exact Farkas certificates, and LP-feasibility monotonicity certify optimal code distances.
FIG. 2. Spherical spin-Wigner functions WP (θ, ϕ) for rank- two projectors: (a,b) aligned numerical and exact n = 22 2D5 codes; (c) exact n = 15 2T code; (d) exact n = 28 2O code with d = 6.

FIG. 3. Rank-two distance phase diagram. Each cell shows feasibility of the intrinsic SU(2) MacWilliams linear-programming bound for total photon number n and loss distance d: blue cells are LP feasible, whereas hatched orange cells are excluded by exact Farkas certificates. The dark blue line marks the boundary between feasible and infeasible regions. LP feasibility is necessary, but not sufficient, for an actual code. Green markers show constructed codes at dcon and are labeled by their construction group; an outer green ring indicates dcon = dF, where dF is the largest LP-feasible distance.
